lines.text: Many learners say: In my city have many parks.
Better: In my city there are many parks.
To say what exists, use there are.
There are! In my city there are many parks.

data.wrong: In my city have many parks.
data.right: In my city there are many parks.
data.why: To say what exists, use there are.

native.tip: “Hay” viene de “haber”, pero en inglés no se usa “have”: es “there is” o “there are.”

en.tip: In English, “hay” is not “have”: it is “there is” or “there are.”
en.caption: Common mistake: “In my city have many parks.” To say something exists in a place, use “there are”: “In my city there are many parks.” Listen to Carlos and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
